title: 三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮
subtitle: 会转弯的小花车
origin: 常用谚语；依据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 好点子不只来自一个人。愿意倾听、一起试验，能把不同的想法变成共同的办法。
moral.en: Listen to one another, test ideas, and build a solution together.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻普通人共同商量、集思广益，也能想出高明的办法；“臭皮匠”在这里是旧时的自谦说法。
idiomMeaning.en: Ordinary people can find wise solutions by thinking together.

visualAnchor: Handcrafted woodland village in spring. Piglet: pink pig, blue overalls, cream shirt. Duckling: yellow duck, green vest, orange feet. Hedgehog: small brown hedgehog, burgundy scarf. Their LOW wooden flower wagon has FOUR solid wooden wheels, a flat rectangular deck, pink and yellow paper flowers, no roof; front two wheels share a pivoting axle only AFTER the redesign. Cobbled lane has a sharp bend between two low stone walls. Keep these designs identical across the book.

pages.zh: 村里的花车游行快到了，小猪、小鸭和小刺猬决定一起造辆小花车。
pages.en: The village parade was coming. Piglet, Duckling, and Hedgehog decided to build a flower wagon together.
pages.prompt: Wide village workshop; all three gather around a simple wagon sketch and loose wooden parts; no completed wagon.

pages.zh: 小猪搬来木板，小鸭画好花样，小刺猬把零件摆得整整齐齐。
pages.en: Piglet brought the boards, Duckling drew the flowers, and Hedgehog arranged the parts in neat rows.
pages.prompt: Workshop overhead view; three friends sort boards, paper flower designs, four solid wheels.

pages.zh: 他们请木匠伯伯帮忙，装好车板和轮子，再系上漂亮的纸花。
pages.en: With the carpenter’s help, they fitted the deck and wheels, then tied on bright paper flowers.
pages.prompt: Adult beaver carpenter assembles the simple wagon; three children attach paper flowers; tools with adult only.

pages.zh: “出发！”小猪轻轻推车，纸花在阳光下晃呀晃。
pages.en: “Here we go!” Piglet pushed gently, and the paper flowers bobbed in the sunshine.
pages.prompt: Finished low four-wheel wagon rolls straight along wide cobbled lane; three friends happy.

pages.zh: 到了石墙边的窄弯，车头过去了，长长的车身却转不过去。
pages.en: At a tight bend between stone walls, the front slipped through, but the long deck could not turn.
pages.prompt: Wide overhead view of wagon stuck diagonally at sharp stone-wall corner; intact wagon and walls; no collision damage.

pages.zh: 小猪又推了一下，车轮还是不动。“先停停！”小刺猬喊道。
pages.en: Piglet pushed once more, but the wheels stayed still. “Let’s stop!” called Hedgehog.
pages.prompt: Piglet stops behind wagon; Hedgehog raises one paw; Duckling looks at narrow corner.

pages.zh: 小鸭说：“换条宽路吧！”可那条路正挖沟，今天不能走。
pages.en: “Let’s take the wider road,” said Duckling. But that road was being repaired and was closed for the day.
pages.prompt: Three friends observe safely from behind a simple wooden barrier; wide alternate lane under repair, wagon parked away.

pages.zh: 小刺猬提议把车做短一些。小猪却舍不得拆掉刚装好的车板。
pages.en: Hedgehog suggested a shorter wagon. Piglet did not want to take apart the deck they had just finished.
pages.prompt: Workshop; Hedgehog gestures along long deck; Piglet rests paw protectively on it; Duckling listens.

pages.zh: “我的办法最好！”“我的也有用！”三个人越说越急。
pages.en: “My idea is best!” “Mine could work too!” Their voices grew louder and louder.
pages.prompt: Three friends talking animatedly around parked wagon, mild frustration not aggression.

pages.zh: 小鸭垂下翅膀：“我们都在说，可谁也没听清。”
pages.en: Duckling lowered her wings. “We’re all talking, but none of us is really listening.”
pages.prompt: Close Duckling lowering wings; Piglet and Hedgehog fall quiet in workshop.

pages.zh: 他们坐到树下，约定轮流说：想改什么，为什么，又担心什么。
pages.en: They sat beneath a tree and took turns explaining their ideas, reasons, and worries.
pages.prompt: Three friends sit in circle under tree, each listening; blank sketch sheets on ground.

pages.zh: 小猪说：“我希望车结实。”小刺猬说：“我希望它转得过弯。”
pages.en: “I want it to be strong,” said Piglet. “I want it to get around the corner,” said Hedgehog.
pages.prompt: Piglet gestures to sturdy wood sample; Hedgehog gestures to simple curved path sketch; Duckling attentive.

pages.zh: 小鸭在地上画出弯道：“先做一辆小小的，试试看吧。”
pages.en: Duckling drew the bend on the ground. “Let’s try a tiny model first.”
pages.prompt: Duckling traces L-shaped corner in sandy ground with stick; others gather small blocks.

pages.zh: 他们用积木搭石墙，用小纸盒当花车。纸盒果然也卡住了。
pages.en: They made walls from blocks and used a small cardboard box as the wagon. It got stuck too.
pages.prompt: Overhead tabletop; miniature long cardboard wagon jammed at L-shaped block walls; three friends' paws nearby.

pages.zh: 小刺猬换上短一点的纸盒。车身能挪动了，可轮子还不肯转弯。
pages.en: Hedgehog tried a shorter box. There was more room now, but the wheels still would not steer.
pages.prompt: Small shorter cardboard model between block walls; front wheels still straight, Hedgehog studying.

pages.zh: 小鸭拨动前轮：“要是这两个轮子能一起转向呢？”
pages.en: Duckling nudged the front wheels. “What if these two wheels could turn together?”
pages.prompt: Close miniature wagon; Duckling rotates shared front axle left with wingtip, clear mechanical pivot.

pages.zh: 小猪找来小圆片和木棒。他们做出能转向的前轴，再试了一遍。
pages.en: Piglet found a small disc and a wooden rod. Together they made a turning front axle and tried again.
pages.prompt: Three friends test miniature wagon with clearly pivoted front axle at block corner.

pages.zh: 小模型顺利绕过弯道！三个脑袋挤在一起，笑出了声。
pages.en: The tiny wagon went around the bend! Three heads leaned close, and three happy laughs rang out.
pages.prompt: Overhead miniature wagon has cleared block corner, friends laugh with relief.

pages.zh: 木匠伯伯照着模型帮忙改车：车板短一些，前轮也能转向了。
pages.en: The carpenter helped them follow the model: a shorter deck and front wheels that could steer.
pages.prompt: Adult beaver adjusts full-size wagon at workshop; shorter deck, pivoting front axle; children observe safely.

pages.zh: 这回到了窄弯，小猪慢推，小鸭引路，小刺猬留意车轮。
pages.en: This time Piglet pushed slowly, Duckling guided the way, and Hedgehog watched the wheels.
pages.prompt: Wide overhead narrow stone corner; shorter flower wagon turning successfully, each friend has clear role.

pages.zh: 花车稳稳地转了过去，大家一起欢呼：“我们做到啦！”
pages.en: The wagon rolled smoothly around the bend. “We did it!” they cheered together.
pages.prompt: Wagon fully beyond stone-wall bend, all three cheering; colorful paper flowers intact.

pages.zh: 游行中，三位朋友并肩走着。小花车上，装着他们一起想出的好办法。
pages.en: In the parade, the three friends walked side by side. Their little wagon carried an idea they had made together.
pages.prompt: Celebratory village parade; three friends together beside small low flower wagon with pivoting front wheels.

title: 磨刀不误砍柴工
subtitle: 小兔的剪纸灯会
origin: 常用谚语；依据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 准备、练习和检查工具都值得花时间。找到合适的方法，再耐心动手，事情会更顺利。
moral.en: Good preparation and suitable tools help us work with care.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻先做好准备、改进工具或方法，可以让后面的工作更顺利。故事借剪纸说明寓意，不涉及孩子磨刀。
idiomMeaning.en: Time spent preparing well can make the work go more smoothly.

visualAnchor: Warm cottage craft room and village courtyard at dusk. Rabbit: small white rabbit with peach inner ears, teal pinafore over cream shirt. Mother Rabbit: taller white rabbit, lavender apron. Mouse friend: tiny gray mouse, yellow sweater. Thick ochre wooden craft table; red, gold and blue craft paper, blunt rounded-tip child scissors, five-point star cardboard template, pencil; lanterns are safe enclosed electric lights, no flames.

pages.zh: 今晚村里要办灯会，小兔想剪一百颗纸星星，把院子装扮得亮亮的。
pages.en: The village lantern evening was coming. Rabbit wanted to cut one hundred paper stars to brighten the courtyard.
pages.prompt: Morning craft room; Rabbit imagines paper-star garlands while looking out at undecorated courtyard.

pages.zh: 她抱来一大摞彩纸，刚坐稳，就拿起剪刀咔嚓咔嚓剪起来。
pages.en: She brought a tall stack of colored paper and began snipping as soon as she sat down.
pages.prompt: Rabbit seated safely cutting single paper sheet with rounded-tip scissors at table; uncut stack beside.

pages.zh: 第一颗星星少了一个角，第二颗又瘦又歪，第三颗一打开就散了。
pages.en: The first star lost a point. The second was thin and crooked. The third fell apart when she unfolded it.
pages.prompt: Close tabletop with three visibly flawed paper-star attempts; Rabbit puzzled.

pages.zh: 地上的碎纸越来越多，桌上的好星星却只有两颗。
pages.en: More and more scraps covered the floor, but only two good stars lay on the table.
pages.prompt: Wide room, scattered paper scraps, exactly two completed five-point stars on table, Rabbit concerned.

pages.zh: 小老鼠来帮忙，看见小兔皱着眉，便轻声问：“哪里不顺手呀？”
pages.en: Mouse came to help. Seeing Rabbit frown, he gently asked, “Which part is giving you trouble?”
pages.prompt: Mouse arrives beside seated Rabbit, looks at paper scraps and scissors.

pages.zh: “剪刀总夹纸！”小兔使劲捏了一下，纸边又被扯破了。
pages.en: “The scissors keep catching!” Rabbit squeezed harder, and the edge of the paper tore again.
pages.prompt: Close rounded-tip scissors catching wrinkled paper; Rabbit hands safely positioned.

pages.zh: 妈妈走过来：“先把剪刀放下，我们一起看看。”
pages.en: Mother came over. “Put the scissors down first. Let’s take a look together.”
pages.prompt: Mother Rabbit calmly joins craft table; Rabbit places closed scissors flat on table.

pages.zh: 原来刀口粘着干胶。妈妈清理、检查后，又试剪了一小条纸。
pages.en: Dried glue had stuck to the blades. Mother cleaned and checked them, then tested them on a strip of paper.
pages.prompt: Mother alone handles scissors and cleaning cloth, children observe; small test strip on table, no sharpening.

pages.zh: 小兔望着窗外：“准备这么久，星星会不会来不及呀？”
pages.en: Rabbit looked out of the window. “If we spend so long getting ready, will we finish in time?”
pages.prompt: Rabbit glances at bright afternoon window, craft supplies neatly waiting.

pages.zh: “先试出一个好办法。”妈妈递来纸板，让小兔画一颗满意的星星。
pages.en: “Let’s find a method that works.” Mother offered cardboard for Rabbit to draw a star she liked.
pages.prompt: Rabbit draws five-point star outline on cardboard; Mother encourages; Mouse watches.

pages.zh: 小兔改了两次，终于画好。妈妈帮她把硬纸板剪成了样板。
pages.en: Rabbit tried twice until she liked the shape. Mother helped cut the stiff cardboard into a template.
pages.prompt: Mother cuts cardboard template; Rabbit displays pencil drafts, Mouse sorts colored sheets.

pages.zh: 小老鼠扶住样板，小兔沿着边描，一颗清楚的星星出现在彩纸上。
pages.en: Mouse held the template still while Rabbit traced around it. A clear star appeared on the colored paper.
pages.prompt: Overhead Mouse holds five-point template flat, Rabbit traces with pencil, scissors closed aside.

pages.zh: 这一次，小兔慢慢剪，转动纸张，一颗完整的星星落在手心里。
pages.en: This time Rabbit cut slowly and turned the paper. A whole star settled into her palm.
pages.prompt: Rabbit holds one clean gold five-point paper star; rounded scissors safely resting on table.

pages.zh: “成啦！”她没有马上抢着多剪，而是先把纸、样板和小筐摆好。
pages.en: “It worked!” Instead of rushing ahead, she arranged the paper, template, and small baskets first.
pages.prompt: Rabbit organizes table into colored paper stack, template, finished-star basket and scrap basket.

pages.zh: 小老鼠描线，小兔剪纸，妈妈把剪好的星星穿在棉线上。
pages.en: Mouse traced, Rabbit cut, and Mother threaded the finished stars onto cotton string.
pages.prompt: Three work calmly at table with distinct tasks; completed star garland growing, no extra characters.

pages.zh: 剪到手酸时，他们停下来伸伸胳膊，喝口水，再接着做。
pages.en: When their hands grew tired, they stretched, drank some water, and then carried on.
pages.prompt: All three pause with water cups and stretching; closed scissors on table, stars in basket.

pages.zh: 小兔发现，不用一百颗也很好看。她把星星疏疏地排开，留下灯光的位置。
pages.en: Rabbit discovered that fewer than one hundred looked lovely too. She spaced the stars apart, leaving room for the lights.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Mouse arrange spaced paper stars along garland; Mother holds enclosed electric lantern nearby, unlit.

pages.zh: 太阳快落山时，星星挂好了。微风一吹，金的、红的、蓝的轻轻摇晃。
pages.en: By sunset the stars were hanging. Gold, red, and blue shapes swayed gently in the breeze.
pages.prompt: Wide courtyard sunset; Mother on ground attaches reachable garland, children admire; safe electric lanterns.

pages.zh: 灯亮起来，小兔拉着小老鼠钻进星光下面：“这里还有你画的那颗！”
pages.en: The lights came on. Rabbit led Mouse beneath the stars. “There’s the one you traced!”
pages.prompt: Dusk courtyard glowing electric lanterns, Rabbit and Mouse point to five-point paper star overhead.

pages.zh: 妈妈说：“磨刀不误砍柴工。”小兔笑了：“原来准备好，也是往前走。”
pages.en: “Good preparation helps the work along,” said Mother. Rabbit smiled. “Getting ready is a way of moving forward too.”
pages.prompt: Warm final wide courtyard, Mother Rabbit and two friends sit together beneath spaced star garland and electric lights.

title: 远水救不了近火
subtitle: 小兔花园里的急事
origin: 常用谚语；依据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 遇到急事，先寻找安全、及时、能解决眼前问题的办法，再为以后做好准备。
moral.en: Choose help that can arrive in time, then prepare for the future.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻距离太远、来不及到达的帮助，不能解决眼前的急难；这里用花苗缺水来说明。
idiomMeaning.en: Distant help cannot solve an urgent problem if it arrives too late.

visualAnchor: Sunny summer cottage garden with rectangular raised bed of newly transplanted small cosmos seedlings. Garden Rabbit: white rabbit with floppy left ear, green dungarees and straw sunhat. Squirrel friend: russet squirrel, blue waistcoat. Goat neighbor: adult cream goat, terracotta apron. Gray watering can, small blue household water jug, pale beige shade cloth on four simple wooden stakes. Distant hills contain spring; no fire in this story. Leaves wilt mildly without dying; flowers only appear in final later scene.

pages.zh: 小兔把花苗移进了新花坛，盼着夏天开出一片粉红色的小花。
pages.en: Rabbit moved young plants into a new garden bed, hoping for a summer full of pink flowers.
pages.prompt: Early morning Rabbit plants small green seedlings in rectangular raised bed; no flowers yet.

pages.zh: 第二天下午，太阳火辣辣的。花苗低着头，叶子软软地垂下来。
pages.en: The next afternoon was very hot. The seedlings bowed their heads, their soft leaves drooping.
pages.prompt: Afternoon overhead bed, mildly wilted green seedlings under bright sunshine, Rabbit notices.

pages.zh: 小兔摸摸泥土：“干了，得给它们浇水！”
pages.en: Rabbit touched the soil. “It’s dry. They need water!”
pages.prompt: Close Rabbit checks dry soil gently with paw, drooping seedlings visible.

pages.zh: 可花园里的水缸见了底，水龙头也因为修管子暂时停水。
pages.en: But the garden water jar was empty, and the tap was off while the village pipes were being repaired.
pages.prompt: Rabbit peers into empty clay garden jar beside closed tap; distant adult repair worker outside garden.

pages.zh: “山上的泉水最清！”小兔提起水壶，“我去打一壶回来。”
pages.en: “The spring in the hills has the clearest water!” Rabbit lifted the watering can. “I’ll fetch some.”
pages.prompt: Rabbit picks up gray empty watering can, looks toward far hills beyond gate.

pages.zh: 小松鼠拦在门边：“那里很远呀，走过去再回来，要好久呢。”
pages.en: Squirrel paused at the gate. “That’s a long way. It will take ages to go there and back.”
pages.prompt: Squirrel beside garden gate gently speaks to Rabbit; distant hills across broad valley.

pages.zh: 小兔看看山，又看看垂着头的花苗，脚步慢了下来。
pages.en: Rabbit looked at the hills, then at the drooping plants, and slowed to a stop.
pages.prompt: Rabbit between gate and garden bed, concerned gaze returns to plants; no journey underway.

pages.zh: “先找附近能用的水吧。”小松鼠说，“还可以想办法遮遮太阳。”
pages.en: “Let’s look for water nearby first,” said Squirrel. “And find some shade for them.”
pages.prompt: Two friends discuss beside bed, Squirrel gestures toward cottage and strong sunlight.

pages.zh: 他们请山羊阿姨帮忙。阿姨先看了看花苗，又摸了摸土。
pages.en: They asked Goat for help. She checked the seedlings and gently felt the soil.
pages.prompt: Adult Goat kneels inspecting bed with Rabbit and Squirrel listening.

pages.zh: “先搭个遮阳棚，让它们少晒一会儿。”阿姨从屋里取来浅色布。
pages.en: “Let’s give them shade first.” Goat brought a pale cloth from her house.
pages.prompt: Goat carries folded beige cloth and wooden stakes toward raised bed; friends help carry cloth only.

pages.zh: 木杆插稳了，布棚撑起来了。棚顶高高的，四周都能透风。
pages.en: The stakes stood firmly, and the cloth went up. It was high enough for air to flow beneath it.
pages.prompt: Complete simple shade cloth above bed on four stable wooden stakes; open sides, all three checking.

pages.zh: 小兔想起厨房里还有一小壶干净的存水，赶紧和妈妈说了花园的事。
pages.en: Rabbit remembered a small jug of clean stored water in the kitchen and told Mother about the garden.
pages.prompt: Rabbit talks to taller white mother rabbit in cream apron beside blue jug on cottage kitchen counter.

pages.zh: 妈妈留好家里要喝的水，把能分出来的那一点倒进小水壶。
pages.en: Mother set aside the water the family needed to drink and poured a little extra into the watering can.
pages.prompt: Mother pours blue jug's spare clean water into gray can; separate covered drinking water bottle safely reserved.

pages.zh: 山羊阿姨扶着壶嘴，小兔慢慢浇，让水落在根边的泥土上。
pages.en: Goat guided the spout as Rabbit watered slowly, letting the water soak into the soil around the roots.
pages.prompt: Close Goat guides gray can held by Rabbit; thin stream lands on soil near stems under shade, not leaves.

pages.zh: 水不多，他们先照顾最缺水的几株，再把剩下的分给其他花苗。
pages.en: There was not much water. They tended the driest plants first, then shared the rest among the others.
pages.prompt: Rabbit and Goat carefully water successive small seedlings; dark moist root circles; Squirrel watches.

pages.zh: “还没有抬头呢。”小兔蹲着等。阿姨说：“先让它们缓一缓。”
pages.en: “They’re still drooping,” said Rabbit, waiting beside them. “Give them time to recover,” said Goat.
pages.prompt: Rabbit sits beside shaded bed, plants still gently drooping despite moist soil, Goat reassuring.

pages.zh: 傍晚凉快了，有几片叶子慢慢挺起来。小兔终于松了一口气。
pages.en: As the evening cooled, a few leaves began to lift. Rabbit finally let out a relieved breath.
pages.prompt: Evening shaded garden, some leaves visibly perk up, Rabbit smiles softly; no flowers yet.

pages.zh: “远水救不了近火。”阿姨说，“今天先用上了来得及的办法。”
pages.en: “Distant water cannot put out a nearby fire,” said Goat. “Today we found help that could arrive in time.”
pages.prompt: Goat and Rabbit at gate look back at recovering bed, distant hills hazy; absolutely no fire imagery.

pages.zh: 水管修好后，小兔请妈妈准备了带盖的储水桶，还画了一张浇水提醒图。
pages.en: When the pipes were fixed, Rabbit and Mother set up a covered water barrel and made a watering reminder picture.
pages.prompt: Mother secures lid on rain barrel; Rabbit draws simple sun-and-watering-can icon card without lettering; healthy green plants.

pages.zh: 过了些日子，小花终于开了。花坛旁的小水壶，已经装好了明早要用的水。
pages.en: Some days later, the flowers finally bloomed. Beside the bed, the little can was ready for the next morning.
pages.prompt: Final later-day garden with modest pink cosmos blooms; Rabbit and Squirrel admire, gray can ready and covered barrel nearby.

title: 路遥知马力，日久见人心
subtitle: 一路上的好朋友
origin: 常用谚语；依据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 了解朋友需要时间。热情的话语和安静的行动都可能表达关心，也要学习主动关心别人。
moral.en: Friendship becomes clearer through time and shared experiences.

idiomMeaning.zh: 走远路才知道马的耐力，相处久了才能更了解一个人的品性；不能只凭第一印象判断朋友。
idiomMeaning.en: A long journey shows a horse’s strength; time reveals a person’s character.

visualAnchor: Gentle woodland hill trail in late spring over several weeks; safe broad path, small puddles, no cliffs. Deer: young tan deer with white spots, blue satchel, no antlers. Fox: small russet fox with cream muzzle and green scarf. Badger: small gray badger with black-and-white facial stripes, ochre vest. Small boxes of colorful books secured by red cotton cord. Destination is a low tree library on a broad stump with three short steps, circular window and leafy canopy; not a high dangerous treehouse.

pages.zh: 山上的小树屋要变成图书角了，小鹿报名帮忙，每周送一箱书上去。
pages.en: The little treehouse on the hill was becoming a library. Deer volunteered to carry up a box of books each week.
pages.prompt: Deer at village book table beside small box, distant low hill tree library visible.

pages.zh: 小狐狸和小獾也来了。小狐狸笑着说：“一路有我，肯定不闷！”
pages.en: Fox and Badger joined him. “With me along, the journey won’t be dull!” said Fox with a grin.
pages.prompt: Three friends meet at trailhead with small book boxes; Fox gestures warmly, Badger reserved.

pages.zh: 小獾只点点头，蹲下来，把箱子上的绳结重新系紧。
pages.en: Badger simply nodded, crouched down, and tightened the knot around a box.
pages.prompt: Close Badger ties red cord securely around book box, Deer watches, Fox waits.

pages.zh: 小鹿心想：小狐狸真热情，小獾是不是不太愿意和我玩呢？
pages.en: Deer thought Fox seemed friendly. He wondered whether quiet Badger wanted to be friends at all.
pages.prompt: Deer glances between animated Fox and quiet Badger, gentle uncertainty, boxes ready.

pages.zh: 第一次上山，小狐狸讲起蘑菇伞的笑话，小鹿笑得差点忘了脚下的坡。
pages.en: On their first climb, Fox told a joke about a mushroom umbrella. Deer laughed and nearly forgot the uphill path.
pages.prompt: Three friends walking broad gentle slope holding small boxes; Fox tells story, Deer smiling.

pages.zh: 小獾走在后面，不时提醒：“前面有树根，慢一点。”
pages.en: Badger followed behind, occasionally saying, “There’s a root ahead. Take it slowly.”
pages.prompt: Badger points out small root across safe broad path; Deer and Fox step carefully, boxes secure.

pages.zh: 到了树屋，他们把书摆上架。小鹿忙着说笑，没看见小獾把空箱折好了。
pages.en: At the treehouse they shelved the books. Busy chatting, Deer did not notice Badger folding the empty boxes.
pages.prompt: Low cozy tree library interior; Deer and Fox shelving books chatting, Badger folds empty cardboard boxes.

pages.zh: 第二周，箱子装得多了一点。走到半路，小鹿的绳结突然松开了。
pages.en: The next week their boxes were a little fuller. Halfway up, the cord around Deer’s box suddenly slipped loose.
pages.prompt: Broad trail, Deer holds box with loosening red cord and opening bottom, friends nearby.

pages.zh: 几本书滑到草地上。小鹿红着脸：“糟了，都怪我没系好。”
pages.en: A few books slid onto the grass. Deer blushed. “Oh no. I didn’t tie it properly.”
pages.prompt: Books scattered on dry grass beside safe trail, Deer embarrassed, no books ruined.

pages.zh: 小狐狸先蹲下捡书：“别急，书都在，我们一起收。”
pages.en: Fox knelt to gather the books. “Don’t worry. They’re all here. Let’s pick them up together.”
pages.prompt: Fox and Deer kneel retrieving colorful books from grass, reassuring expression.

pages.zh: 小獾拿出备用绳，把箱底托牢，还教小鹿试着打了一个结。
pages.en: Badger took out spare cord, supported the box, and helped Deer practice a secure knot.
pages.prompt: Badger demonstrates knot on repaired box while Deer tries, Fox stacks retrieved books.

pages.zh: 重新出发时，小鹿主动等了等：“小獾，走到我旁边来吧。”
pages.en: When they set off again, Deer waited. “Badger, come and walk beside me.”
pages.prompt: Three friends now walking abreast on broad trail, repaired small box secure.

pages.zh: 第三周下过雨，路边多了几个水洼。小狐狸的话比平时少了。
pages.en: Rain had fallen before their third trip, leaving puddles beside the path. Fox was quieter than usual.
pages.prompt: Overcast woodland path dotted shallow puddles, Fox quiet behind Deer and Badger, no active storm.

pages.zh: 小鹿回过头，发现小狐狸的鞋带松了，一只鞋还进了小石子。
pages.en: Deer looked back and saw Fox’s loose shoelace. A tiny stone had slipped into one shoe too.
pages.prompt: Fox seated on low log safely checking small boot, visible loose lace and tiny pebble; Deer notices.

pages.zh: “先歇一会儿。”小鹿接过他的箱子，小獾找了一块干燥的地方。
pages.en: “Let’s rest.” Deer took Fox’s box, and Badger found a dry place to sit.
pages.prompt: All three at dry log beside trail; Deer sets Fox box safely down, Badger points to comfortable seat.

pages.zh: 小狐狸倒出石子，重新系好鞋带。三个人坐着分吃带来的小饼。
pages.en: Fox shook out the stone and retied his shoe. The three friends sat and shared their little biscuits.
pages.prompt: Three friends sit on dry log sharing biscuits, tied boots, secure book boxes on dry ground.

pages.zh: 小鹿这才发现，爱说笑的朋友也会累，安静的朋友也有好多话想说。
pages.en: Deer began to see that a cheerful friend could get tired, and a quiet friend could have plenty to say.
pages.prompt: Intimate three-friend conversation at log, Badger speaking with gentle animation, others listen.

pages.zh: 小獾说，他最喜欢讲星星的书。小狐狸立刻说：“下次你讲给我们听！”
pages.en: Badger said he loved books about stars. “Tell us about them next time!” said Fox.
pages.prompt: Badger opens illustrated star book with pictorial constellations no text, Fox and Deer interested.

pages.zh: 一周又一周，树屋的书架渐渐满了。他们也越来越懂得照顾彼此。
pages.en: Week after week, the shelves filled up. The friends grew better at looking after one another too.
pages.prompt: One later afternoon in low tree library, much fuller bookshelves, three friends arrange books together; single scene not montage.

pages.zh: 有时小狐狸带路，有时小獾讲故事，有时小鹿提醒大家停下来喝水。
pages.en: Sometimes Fox led, sometimes Badger told stories, and sometimes Deer reminded everyone to stop for water.
pages.prompt: Three friends on trail water break; Deer offers water flask, Badger mid-story, Fox listens; boxes resting.

pages.zh: 图书角开放那天，三位朋友坐在一起。小鹿说：“幸好这一路有你们。”
pages.en: On opening day, the three sat together in the library. “I’m glad you were with me all the way,” said Deer.
pages.prompt: Cozy completed tree library, three friends sit together on low cushions surrounded by books, warm sunlight.

pages.zh: 回家的路还很长，小鹿却不着急。他知道，好朋友是在日子里慢慢认识的。
pages.en: The walk home was still long, but Deer was in no hurry. Good friends, he knew, were discovered over time.
pages.prompt: Final wide sunset trail, Deer Fox Badger walking home side by side, empty folded boxes carried, gentle safe hill.

title: 一寸光阴一寸金，寸金难买寸光阴
subtitle: 小猴的日落约定
origin: 常用谚语；依据谚语寓意创作的原创童话，并非历史典故。

moral.zh: 时间珍贵，尤其是与人相处的时光。给重要的约定留出时间，也能安心享受玩耍。
moral.en: Make time for the people and promises that matter.

idiomMeaning.zh: 形容时间十分宝贵，过去的时间无法用金钱买回来，提醒人珍惜光阴。
idiomMeaning.en: Time is as precious as gold, but gold cannot buy back time that has passed.

visualAnchor: Warm leafy village near a pond, one day from morning to sunset. Monkey: small golden-brown monkey with cream face, coral-red vest, long curled tail. Turtle: small green turtle with olive segmented shell, blue scarf. Turtle Mother: larger green turtle, plum shawl. Monkey drawing supplies: cream drawing paper, short colored pencils in wooden box, simple low table. Turtle family moving with small wooden handcart carrying tied bundles. Portrait only shows turtle by pond with a green reed, and is created after page 12. No written text or clocks with numerals.

pages.zh: 清早，小乌龟告诉小猴：“我们今天搬家，太阳落山前就出发。”
pages.en: That morning Turtle told Monkey, “We’re moving today. We’ll leave before sunset.”
pages.prompt: Morning outside Turtle cottage; Turtle speaks to Monkey, Mother sorts modest bundles by handcart.

pages.zh: 小猴有点舍不得：“我给你画张像吧，把咱们的小池塘也画进去！”
pages.en: Monkey felt sad to say goodbye. “I’ll draw your portrait, with our little pond in it!”
pages.prompt: Monkey and Turtle beside pond smiling tenderly, reeds and lily pads visible.

pages.zh: 小乌龟笑了：“那我们下午一起画，我还能帮你挑颜色。”
pages.en: Turtle smiled. “Let’s draw together this afternoon. I can help you choose the colors.”
pages.prompt: Two friends agree by low outdoor drawing table, closed pencil box and blank paper waiting.

pages.zh: 小猴把纸和画笔摆好，抬头看看太阳：“还早着呢，先玩一会儿。”
pages.en: Monkey set out paper and pencils, then looked up at the sun. “There’s lots of time. I’ll play a little first.”
pages.prompt: Late morning Monkey sets fresh blank cream paper and colored pencils on low table, looks toward sunny garden.

pages.zh: 一只蓝蝴蝶飞过篱笆，小猴跟着跑到草地上，看它停在花瓣间。
pages.en: A blue butterfly flew over the fence. Monkey followed it to the meadow and watched it settle on a flower.
pages.prompt: Monkey watching blue butterfly on meadow flower, curious joyful calm; no drawing supplies here.

pages.zh: 草地真好玩。他滚了两圈，又捡了一颗圆圆的小石子。
pages.en: The meadow was fun. He rolled twice in the grass and found a little round pebble.
pages.prompt: Monkey playfully rolls on soft meadow grass, small smooth pebble nearby, no danger.

pages.zh: 吃过午饭，小猴想起画像，刚走到桌边，又听见池塘边的水声。
pages.en: After lunch Monkey remembered the portrait. He reached the table, then heard splashing by the pond.
pages.prompt: Monkey at low table with still-blank paper, turns toward pond in background.

pages.zh: 他坐在浅浅的岸边，用叶子做小船，一放就是好几只。
pages.en: He sat safely at the shallow edge and floated leaf boats, one after another.
pages.prompt: Monkey seated on dry grassy bank, floats small leaf boats in very shallow pond margin, no swimming.

pages.zh: 小乌龟来找他：“现在画吗？”小猴说：“等这只船漂到那边就来。”
pages.en: “Shall we draw now?” asked Turtle. “As soon as this boat reaches the other side,” said Monkey.
pages.prompt: Turtle arrives beside Monkey on bank, gestures toward distant table; Monkey watches one leaf boat.

pages.zh: 可小船绕着水草打转。等小猴抬起头，小乌龟已经回去帮妈妈了。
pages.en: But the boat circled around the reeds. When Monkey looked up, Turtle had gone home to help Mother.
pages.prompt: Monkey looks up alone from circling leaf boat; Turtle visible farther away walking toward Mother and handcart.

pages.zh: 树影越来越长。村口传来收拾行李的声音，小猴一下子站起来。
pages.en: The tree shadows grew longer. Monkey heard bundles being packed near the gate and suddenly stood up.
pages.prompt: Late-afternoon Monkey rises on dry bank, long shadows, distant family packs wooden handcart.

pages.zh: 桌上的画纸还是空白的。小猴握住画笔，心里又急又难过。
pages.en: The paper on the table was still blank. Monkey held a pencil, feeling hurried and sad.
pages.prompt: Close Monkey at table facing completely blank cream paper, pencil poised, remorse not panic.

pages.zh: 他跑到小乌龟家：“对不起，我让你等了。我们现在还能一起画吗？”
pages.en: He ran to Turtle’s house. “I’m sorry I kept you waiting. Can we still draw together?”
pages.prompt: Monkey speaks apologetically to Turtle beside packed cart, holds blank paper and pencil box.

pages.zh: 小乌龟摇摇头：“我得帮妈妈检查东西了，不过，我还是想收到你的画。”
pages.en: Turtle shook his head. “I have to help Mother check our things. But I’d still love your drawing.”
pages.prompt: Turtle kindly but firmly replies, Mother checks bundles; Monkey listens holding drawing supplies.

pages.zh: 小猴回到桌前，没有再想着画满整张纸。他先画朋友弯弯的笑眼。
pages.en: Monkey returned to the table. He stopped trying to fill the whole page and began with his friend’s smiling eyes.
pages.prompt: Close paper on table with only simple turtle face sketch beginning, Monkey draws attentively.

pages.zh: 接着是圆圆的龟壳、小池塘，还有他们常坐的那片绿草地。
pages.en: Next came the round shell, the pond, and the grassy spot where they often sat together.
pages.prompt: Overhead drawing progresses into simple childlike Turtle portrait by blue pond and green bank, colored pencils around.

pages.zh: 画好了。小猴仔细夹好画纸，赶在出发前送到小乌龟手里。
pages.en: The picture was finished. Monkey protected it between two boards and brought it to Turtle before they left.
pages.prompt: Monkey presents simple finished Turtle-and-pond portrait safely to Turtle beside ready handcart, sunset approaching.

pages.zh: “这里少了一根芦苇。”小乌龟笑着指出来。小猴递过绿笔，让他添上。
pages.en: “It needs one reed here,” Turtle said with a smile. Monkey offered a green pencil so he could add it.
pages.prompt: Close Turtle adds single green reed to finished pond portrait resting on flat board, Monkey holds green-pencil box.

pages.zh: 小猴陪他们走到村口。这一次，他认真听朋友说新家的模样。
pages.en: Monkey walked with the family to the village gate. This time he listened carefully as Turtle described their new home.
pages.prompt: Monkey and Turtle walk beside Mother pulling small handcart toward village gate, Turtle holds protected drawing, warm sunset.

pages.zh: 夕阳照着画像，小猴轻轻挥手。他记住了：重要的约定，要留出真正相处的时间。
pages.en: Sunset warmed the picture as Monkey waved goodbye. He would remember to leave real time for the promises and people he cared about.
pages.prompt: Final Monkey waves from village gate as Turtle family departs slowly on safe path; Turtle waves holding portrait, tender hopeful sunset.
